paragraphs.title: The Fine-Flour Offering and Its Presentation

easy.question: What type of offering is described in these verses?
answers: A grain offering
A sin offering
A Passover offering
easy.explanation: The passage begins, “When anyone will offer a grain offering unto the Lord.”

easy.question: What is poured over the fine flour?
answers: Water
Oil
Wine
easy.explanation: The verse says, “He shall pour oil upon it.”

easy.question: To whom does the portion left from the offering belong?
answers: The person who brought it alone
All the people
Aaron and his sons
easy.explanation: The verse says, “The remnant of the meat offering shall be Aaron’s and his sons’.”

medium.question: What does the priest do after the offering is brought to him?
answers: He takes a handful and burns it on the altar
He returns it to the person who brought it
He eats all of it immediately
medium.explanation: The priest takes a handful of the flour and oil, along with the frankincense, and burns the memorial portion on the altar.

medium.question: In the phrase “he shall take thereout his handful,” what action is being described?
answers: Pouring out everything
Taking a handful
Mixing it with water
medium.explanation: The phrase means that the priest takes a quantity that fits in his hand.

medium.question: What is done with the part of the offering that is not burned on the altar?
answers: It is all burned
It is buried outside the camp
It is given to Aaron and his sons
medium.explanation: The remaining portion belongs to Aaron and his sons.

challenge.question: What does the priest burn according to the description?
answers: A handful of the flour and oil, together with all the frankincense
All the flour alone
Only the frankincense, without flour or oil
challenge.explanation: The priest takes a handful of the flour and oil, together with all the frankincense, and burns the memorial portion.

challenge.question: What does the expression “a thing most holy” indicate about the remaining offering?
answers: That it is ordinary food
That it has a high degree of holiness
That it is available without restriction to everyone
challenge.explanation: The expression identifies the remaining offering as especially holy.

challenge.question: What distinguishes this offering from an animal sacrifice?
answers: It is offered only at night
It is eaten by all Israel
It is made from fine flour, oil, and frankincense
challenge.explanation: The offering consists of plant-based ingredients rather than an animal.

questions.question: What does the priest burn according to the description?
answers: A handful of the flour and oil, together with all the frankincense
All the flour alone
Only the frankincense, without flour or oil
questions.explanation: The priest takes a handful of the flour and oil, together with all the frankincense, and burns the memorial portion.

questions.question: What does the expression “a thing most holy” indicate about the remaining offering?
answers: That it is ordinary food
That it has a high degree of holiness
That it is available without restriction to everyone
questions.explanation: The expression identifies the remaining offering as especially holy.

questions.question: What distinguishes this offering from an animal sacrifice?
answers: It is offered only at night
It is eaten by all Israel
It is made from fine flour, oil, and frankincense
questions.explanation: The offering consists of plant-based ingredients rather than an animal.

easy.question: In what is the offering in verse 4 baked?
answers: An oven
A pan
A frying pan
easy.explanation: Verse 4 describes an offering baked in an oven.

easy.question: Which ingredient is mixed with or spread over the flour in several types of offerings?
answers: Honey
Oil
Salt
easy.explanation: The verses repeatedly require oil to be mixed with or spread over the offering.

easy.question: What is said about the offering in verse 5?
answers: It must be leavened
It must be without oil
It must be unleavened
easy.explanation: Verse 5 says that it shall be unleavened.

medium.question: What is done to the offering baked in a pan after it is prepared?
answers: It is divided into pieces and oil is poured over it
Honey and salt are added
It is baked again in an oven
medium.explanation: The verse says, “Thou shalt part it in pieces, and pour oil thereon.”

medium.question: What does the verse say about the fine flour in the pan offering?
answers: It is mixed with oil
It is burned in oil
It is covered with salt
medium.explanation: The verse describes the flour as being mingled with oil.

medium.question: What is the main difference between the pan offering and the frying-pan offering?
answers: The pan offering is divided into pieces, while the frying-pan offering is made from flour with oil
The pan offering is baked in an oven, while the frying-pan offering contains honey
The pan offering is leavened, while the frying-pan offering is unleavened
medium.explanation: The pan offering is divided into pieces, while the frying-pan offering is simply described as fine flour made with oil.

challenge.question: What feature is shared by the three types of offerings described in these verses?
answers: They include oil and are unleavened
They are all baked in an oven
They are all made from leavened bread
challenge.explanation: The descriptions include oil, and the offerings are specified to be unleavened.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the references to an oven, a pan, and a frying pan?
answers: There are several possible methods of preparing this type of offering
Only the last offering is considered a grain offering
Each utensil requires completely different ingredients
challenge.explanation: The verses present different preparation methods and utensils for the same general type of offering.

challenge.question: What detail distinguishes the two oven-baked products in verse 4?
answers: One is unleavened cakes mixed with oil, and the other is unleavened wafers spread with oil
One is leavened and the other is unleavened
One is boiled in water and the other is fried in honey
challenge.explanation: Verse 4 mentions unleavened cakes mixed with oil and unleavened wafers anointed with oil.

questions.question: What feature is shared by the three types of offerings described in these verses?
answers: They include oil and are unleavened
They are all baked in an oven
They are all made from leavened bread
questions.explanation: The descriptions include oil, and the offerings are specified to be unleavened.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the references to an oven, a pan, and a frying pan?
answers: There are several possible methods of preparing this type of offering
Only the last offering is considered a grain offering
Each utensil requires completely different ingredients
questions.explanation: The verses present different preparation methods and utensils for the same general type of offering.

questions.question: What detail distinguishes the two oven-baked products in verse 4?
answers: One is unleavened cakes mixed with oil, and the other is unleavened wafers spread with oil
One is leavened and the other is unleavened
One is boiled in water and the other is fried in honey
questions.explanation: Verse 4 mentions unleavened cakes mixed with oil and unleavened wafers anointed with oil.

easy.question: To whom is the offering brought?
answers: To the Lord
To the king
To the people
easy.explanation: The verse says that the offering is brought to the Lord.

easy.question: Who brings the offering to the altar?
answers: The person who brought the offering
The priest
Aaron alone
easy.explanation: The priest presents the offering and brings it to the altar.

easy.question: To whom does the part left over belong?
answers: All Israel
The person who brought it alone
Aaron and his sons
easy.explanation: The remaining offering belongs to Aaron and his sons.

medium.question: What does the priest do with part of the offering before the remainder is given to Aaron and his sons?
answers: He burns it on the altar
He returns it to the person who brought it
He keeps it outside the sanctuary
medium.explanation: The priest takes a memorial portion and burns it on the altar; the remainder belongs to Aaron and his sons.

medium.question: In the phrase “the priest shall take from the meat offering a memorial thereof,” what is the priest taking?
answers: A sacred utensil
A portion set apart from the offering
A song sung in the sanctuary
medium.explanation: The phrase refers to the portion of the offering that the priest sets apart and burns on the altar.

medium.question: What is the order of actions described in the verses?
answers: The remainder is given to the priest, and then the offering is brought
The offering is brought, the priest takes and burns part of it, and the remainder is given to Aaron and his sons
The priest eats the whole offering, and then part of it is burned
medium.explanation: First the offering is brought, then the priest burns its memorial portion, and finally the remainder belongs to Aaron and his sons.

challenge.question: What distinction between the portions of the offering is made in these verses?
answers: One portion is burned for the Lord, and the remainder is given to Aaron and his sons
The whole offering is given to Aaron and his sons
The whole offering is burned on the altar
challenge.explanation: The priest burns the memorial portion, while the remainder is assigned to Aaron and his sons.

challenge.question: What does the expression “an offering made by fire, of a sweet savour unto the Lord” indicate?
answers: That the offering was burned accidentally
That the burning is described as a pleasing act before the Lord
That the offering was meant to spread fragrance only for people
challenge.explanation: The expression presents the offering as a pleasing act of worship before the Lord.

challenge.question: What does “a thing most holy” emphasize about the remainder?
answers: That it is ordinary food usable anywhere
That it belongs to every Israelite
That it is highly holy and assigned to Aaron and his sons
challenge.explanation: The remainder is not ordinary food; it is a most holy portion designated for the priests.

questions.question: What distinction between the portions of the offering is made in these verses?
answers: One portion is burned for the Lord, and the remainder is given to Aaron and his sons
The whole offering is given to Aaron and his sons
The whole offering is burned on the altar
questions.explanation: The priest burns the memorial portion, while the remainder is assigned to Aaron and his sons.

questions.question: What does the expression “an offering made by fire, of a sweet savour unto the Lord” indicate?
answers: That the offering was burned accidentally
That the burning is described as a pleasing act before the Lord
That the offering was meant to spread fragrance only for people
questions.explanation: The expression presents the offering as a pleasing act of worship before the Lord.

questions.question: What does “a thing most holy” emphasize about the remainder?
answers: That it is ordinary food usable anywhere
That it belongs to every Israelite
That it is highly holy and assigned to Aaron and his sons
questions.explanation: The remainder is not ordinary food; it is a most holy portion designated for the priests.

paragraphs.title: The Prohibitions of Leaven and Honey and the Salt of the Covenant

easy.question: What may not be used in any grain offering brought to the Lord?
answers: Leaven
Salt
Firstfruits
easy.explanation: The verse says that no grain offering brought to the Lord may be made with leaven.

easy.question: With what does the passage command every grain offering to be seasoned?
answers: Honey
Salt
Leaven
easy.explanation: The verse says, “With all thine offerings thou shalt offer salt.”

easy.question: What may not be burned on the altar as part of the offering?
answers: Salt and firstfruits
Oil and fine flour
Leaven and honey
easy.explanation: The verse says that no leaven or honey is to be burned in an offering made by fire.

medium.question: What is the correct order of the instructions in these verses?
answers: The prohibition of leaven, the rule about firstfruits, and the command concerning salt
The command concerning salt, the prohibition of honey, and then the rule about firstfruits
The rule about firstfruits, the command to use leaven, and then the prohibition of salt
medium.explanation: The passage first discusses leaven and honey, then firstfruits, and finally salt.

medium.question: What does the verse mean by “leaven” in the phrase “ye shall burn no leaven”?
answers: A substance that makes dough rise
Salt that preserves the offering
A sweet fruit brought to the sanctuary
medium.explanation: Leaven is a substance used to make dough rise.

medium.question: What is the difference between a firstfruits offering and an offering burned on the altar?
answers: A firstfruits offering may be presented to the Lord, but it may not be burned on the altar as a sweet savour
A firstfruits offering may not be presented at all
A firstfruits offering must be made with leaven
medium.explanation: The passage permits the firstfruits offering to be presented to the Lord but says it must not be burned on the altar for a sweet savour.

challenge.question: What principle concerning salt, leaven, and honey appears in these verses?
answers: All three are required in every offering
All three may be eaten only by the priests
Salt is required, while leaven and honey are not burned
challenge.explanation: Salt is required with the offerings, whereas leaven and honey are prohibited from being burned.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the statement “with all thine offerings thou shalt offer salt”?
answers: Salt is an important part of every kind of offering
Salt is permitted only in grain offerings
Salt takes the place of leaven and honey
challenge.explanation: The statement extends the requirement for salt to all offerings, not only grain offerings.

challenge.question: Which distinction is accurately expressed by the passage?
answers: Everything presented to the Lord must be burned on the altar
Something may be presented to the Lord without being burned on the altar as a sweet savour
Nothing containing salt may be presented to the Lord
challenge.explanation: The firstfruits may be presented to the Lord but are specifically not to be burned on the altar as a sweet savour.

questions.question: What principle concerning salt, leaven, and honey appears in these verses?
answers: All three are required in every offering
All three may be eaten only by the priests
Salt is required, while leaven and honey are not burned
questions.explanation: Salt is required with the offerings, whereas leaven and honey are prohibited from being burned.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the statement “with all thine offerings thou shalt offer salt”?
answers: Salt is an important part of every kind of offering
Salt is permitted only in grain offerings
Salt takes the place of leaven and honey
questions.explanation: The statement extends the requirement for salt to all offerings, not only grain offerings.

questions.question: Which distinction is accurately expressed by the passage?
answers: Everything presented to the Lord must be burned on the altar
Something may be presented to the Lord without being burned on the altar as a sweet savour
Nothing containing salt may be presented to the Lord
questions.explanation: The firstfruits may be presented to the Lord but are specifically not to be burned on the altar as a sweet savour.

easy.question: To whom is the firstfruits offering presented?
answers: To the Lord
To the king
To the people
easy.explanation: The passage says, “Thou shalt offer for the meat offering of thy firstfruits” to the Lord.

easy.question: What is placed on the firstfruits offering?
answers: Blood and water
Oil and frankincense
Salt and honey
easy.explanation: The verse says, “Thou shalt put oil upon it, and lay frankincense thereon.”

easy.question: Who burns the memorial portion of the offering?
answers: The king
The person who brought it
The priest
easy.explanation: The verse explicitly says, “The priest shall burn the memorial of it.”

medium.question: Why are both oil and frankincense mentioned in connection with the offering?
answers: To describe the sanctuary vessels
Because they are placed on the offering and included in its presentation
To replace the grain
medium.explanation: The passage instructs that oil and frankincense be placed on the offering and then describes the burning of part of it.

medium.question: What is meant by “green ears of corn dried by the fire”?
answers: A tool used to measure grain
New grain roasted or dried by fire
A plant that grows in the wilderness
medium.explanation: The phrase describes fresh grain that has been dried or roasted by fire.

medium.question: What is the order of actions described in these verses?
answers: Oil and frankincense are placed on the offering, and then the priest burns part of it
The priest burns it, and then the grain is roasted
Frankincense is added, and then the grain is brought
medium.explanation: The offering is presented, oil and frankincense are placed on it, and then the priest burns its memorial portion.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the phrase “part of the beaten corn thereof, and part of the oil thereof”?
answers: The priest burns part of the grain and part of the oil, not the entire offering
The oil has no connection with the offering
The grain and oil are eaten before the offering is presented
challenge.explanation: The verse specifies that only part of the grain and part of the oil form the memorial portion.

challenge.question: What special detail is stated about the frankincense?
answers: Only a small amount is placed on the offering
All of it is burned
It may not be burned
challenge.explanation: The verse says that the priest burns the grain and oil together with all the frankincense.

challenge.question: What does “green ears of corn dried by the fire” teach about the grain?
answers: It must be boiled in water
It must be made only from old flour
It is fresh grain that has been dried or roasted by fire
challenge.explanation: The expression refers to new grain prepared by drying or roasting it over a fire.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the phrase “part of the beaten corn thereof, and part of the oil thereof”?
answers: The priest burns part of the grain and part of the oil, not the entire offering
The oil has no connection with the offering
The grain and oil are eaten before the offering is presented
questions.explanation: The verse specifies that only part of the grain and part of the oil form the memorial portion.

questions.question: What special detail is stated about the frankincense?
answers: Only a small amount is placed on the offering
All of it is burned
It may not be burned
questions.explanation: The verse says that the priest burns the grain and oil together with all the frankincense.

questions.question: What does “green ears of corn dried by the fire” teach about the grain?
answers: It must be boiled in water
It must be made only from old flour
It is fresh grain that has been dried or roasted by fire
questions.explanation: The expression refers to new grain prepared by drying or roasting it over a fire.
